stem: A 10 $\\Omega$ resistor is connected across the terminals of a 10 V battery. What is the power dissipation of the resistor?
solution_latex: The power dissipation P of a resistor can be calculated using the formula $P = \\frac{V^2}{R}$, where V is the voltage across the resistor and R is its resistance. Given V = 10 V and R = 10 $\\Omega$, we have $P = \\frac{(10 \\text{ V})^2}{10 \\text{ } \\Omega} = \\frac{100 \\text{ V}^2}{10 \\text{ } \\Omega} = 100 \\text{ W}$.
